record.original_question: Let Homk (Z2 , Homeo0 (R2 )) be the subspace of Z2 -actions on R2 whose Euler number is k. Are subspaces Homk (Z2 , Homeo0 (R2 )) connected for each integer k?

evidence.quote: Question 5.1. Let Homk (Z2 , Homeo0 (R2 )) be the subspace of Z2 -actions on R2 whose Euler number is k. Are subspaces Homk (Z2 , Homeo0 (R2 )) connected for each integer k?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{Homeo}_0(\mathbb{R}^2)$ denote the identity component of the group of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, equipped with the compact-open topology. Let $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}^2,\mathrm{Homeo}_0(\mathbb{R}^2))$ be the space of group homomorphisms $\rho:\mathbb{Z}^2\to\mathrm{Homeo}_0(\mathbb{R}^2)$ (equivalently, the space of $\mathbb{Z}^2$-actions on $\mathbb{R}^2$ by orientation-preserving homeomorphisms isotopic to the identity), endowed with the subspace topology coming from the compact-open topology on the target.

To each such action $\rho$ one can associate an integer-valued invariant, the Euler number $e(\rho)\in\mathbb{Z}$, defined as follows. Choose generators $a,b$ of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ and lifts $\widetilde{\rho(a)},\widetilde{\rho(b)}$ of $\rho(a),\rho(b)$ to homeomorphisms of the universal cover (or to compactly supported lifts in an appropriate sense). The commutator $[\widetilde{\rho(a)},\widetilde{\rho(b)}]$ is a deck transformation, and the Euler number $e(\rho)$ is the corresponding integer. This invariant is locally constant on $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}^2,\mathrm{Homeo}_0(\mathbb{R}^2))$.

For each integer $k$, let
$$\mathrm{Hom}_k(\mathbb{Z}^2,\mathrm{Homeo}_0(\mathbb{R}^2)) := \{\rho\in\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}^2,\mathrm{Homeo}_0(\mathbb{R}^2)) : e(\rho)=k\}.$$

Question: Is the subspace $\mathrm{Hom}_k(\mathbb{Z}^2,\mathrm{Homeo}_0(\mathbb{R}^2))$ path-connected (equivalently, connected) for every integer $k$?
artifact.category_tag: Group actions on surfaces / homeomorphism groups
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any published resolution of this question. Related work (e.g., Kathryn Mann's results on topological components of representation spaces of surface groups) studies connected components of spaces of representations into homeomorphism groups via Euler-number-type invariants, but no source confirming the connectedness of each $\mathrm{Hom}_k(\mathbb{Z}^2,\mathrm{Homeo}_0(\mathbb{R}^2))$ was found. The problem appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Spaces of surface group representations
status_evidence.snippet: Studies connected components of representation spaces into homeomorphism groups using Euler number invariants.
status_evidence.claim: Related context shows Euler-number-indexed components of representation spaces are an active research topic, but the specific Z^2 case on R^2 is not resolved in the visible literature.
